key_terms.إِنَّهَا: It (referring to the gates of Paradise or mercy)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the gates are sealed for the disbelievers?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (often linked to Surah Al-Baqarah 2:70 or Al-Imran 3:86 in broader contexts of sealing) emphasizes the permanence of divine judgment, where the 'sealing' (tawsid) signifies that the hearts of disbelievers have become impervious to truth due to their own choices. This reflects the concept of *khatm* (sealing) as a consequence of *kufr*, ensuring that the gates of mercy remain closed until the Day of Resurrection.
